findings.title: Execution and scoring receipts omit sources that implement the reviewed behavior
findings.problem: The evaluator records thirteen inference source hashes but omits patch_embed.py, whose forward method is actually used by E0. The scorer checks that same limited map and records its own script and toolkit hashes, but neither records nor checks the project helpers implementing official_metrics and LasHeR aggregation. Consequently the produced receipts cannot identify all reviewed numerical code, and changed omitted helpers would not be rejected by the current source-hash checks.
current_repository_evidence: A CUDA-masked import inventory on actual host25 loaded lib/models/layers/patch_embed.py, and the E0 source directly calls trunk.patch_embed for templates and search.
The scoring entry imports official_metrics from tools/joint_candidate_results.py; its LasHeR branch calls scripts/score_tracking.py.

Local joint_candidate_results.py has SHA256 94cee1532d82d2b0cf1d5a3e83c9e3ab11601d89db135e1d8a032962e9661867, while actual host25 has 207ee0e338793db030c1b49bd42a143b347260de6801d915006d898b9dedcc24. Their official_metrics ASTs are equal; the observed differences are outside the called function. This is evidence of real file-version divergence, not a claim that their present metric values differ.
minimal_required_fix: Extend the inference source receipt/check to include patch_embed.py and the imported project dependency set identified in this report.

Record and verify a scoring source map including score_e0_finetuned.py, joint_candidate_results.py, score_tracking.py, benchmark_inputs.py and the imported joint_evaluation_contract.py, using the actual reviewed target versions.

Have the separate launch/admission integration compare those source maps with the review before execution. Preserve existing remote helper/wrapper versions unless separately reviewed; do not replace them merely to match the local checkout.

The reviewer did not load a new finetuned checkpoint or execute the evaluator.

engineering_assessments.area: TRAIN Smoke And Full Test Separation
engineering_assessments.assessment: Only smoke_frames0 or11 is admitted. Smoke requires LasHeR/train_smoke, uses the first sequence and exactly11 frames, and writes SMOKE.json. Full evaluation requires test and245/210/234 sequences. The scorer requires COMPLETE.json, non-smoke, split=test, complete sequence/frame counts and explicit exploratory/test-ineligible flags. The actual checked smoke manifest is train sequence2up; actual LasHeR test names have zero overlap with the882 training names. These guarantees assume the checked manifest hashes are used, not a relabelled arbitrary manifest.

The evaluator checks native RUNNING, parent PID, exact interpreter/argv command and visible GPU. Actual host25 wrapper sets PCI_BUS_ID ordering and the selected GPU before spawning its child and records the real exit code. Scoring requires native COMPLETE/exit0 and matching task/command/GPU across receipts. No native receipt for a new evaluation was produced or accepted by this review.

Initialization receives only initial_box. Every subsequent track call receives the current decoded image; search crops use previous predicted state, and template/history updates use predictions and confidence. Full GT arrays are available to manifest validation and later output, but are not passed to tracker.track, model.predict or online route selection. Direct tracker import retains its original dual_rgbt.data.crop_pair binding; there is no crop monkeypatch or post-import replacement in the new entry.

No-grad evaluation, eval mode and disabled parameter gradients prevent training. Full model state tensors are cloned and compared exactly at the end, and gradients must remain None. Tracker state/templates/history intentionally evolve. TF32 is disabled. Outer timing begins before image decode; tracker synchronizes CUDA at call boundaries, including after template updates. Summed timing includes sequence initialization and decode, excludes model loading and output/GT writes, and is explicitly labelled concurrent-load service timing rather than isolated throughput. No timing measurement was performed by this review.

Manifest names are unique with summed frame counts and matching RGB/thermal/GT lengths. Scoring requires exact prediction filename coverage and expected full dataset names/counts, checks every prediction shape against full GT, finite positive predicted sizes, each saved GT array against the manifest and toolkit, and a full-length positive timing array agreeing with completion seconds. These prechecks occur before the toolkit's own permissive result trimming and prevent shortened predictions from being scored. Expected GT files are all checked; unrelated extra GT files do not enter metrics.

LasHeR uses original PR_LasHeR/NPR/SR_LasHeR, reporting index20 precision and mean success curves, macro-averaged across sequences. RGBT210 uses PR/SR; RGBT234 uses MPR/MSR with the toolkit's visible/infrared semantics. Original toolkit rounding of loaded predictions, first-frame handling and invalid-GT rules are preserved, rather than replaced by a new metric implementation. Seven protocol toolkit hashes match actual host25. Metrics themselves were not run and no benchmark result is accepted.

engineering_assessments.area: Linux Annotation Paths And CPU Imports
engineering_assessments.assessment: Both toolkit-code and annotation paths replace Windows backslashes with Linux separators. On actual host25 cpu-scoring Python, benchmark_inputs, joint_candidate_results, score_tracking, rgbt and metric modules import successfully. The exact new scoring source was also compiled/executed in memory with its main guard disabled and its prospective target __file__; imports passed without deploying it. All211 RGBT210 and469 RGBT234 annotation hashes matched after separator conversion.
